family: Deterministic evidence visual (chart / table / timeline / framework) carrying exact traceable values — the artifact-plan 'evidence_visual' kind.
primary_job: Answer one specific question with inspectable, traceable evidence: exact values, distributions, or exceptions from source data (schemas/artifact-plan.schema.json spec.question; VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md §1 'evidence' gain type).

semantic_density.rationale: The entire purpose is to expose exact patterns, values, or exceptions the reader cannot get from prose alone; overlap with a prose conclusion is acceptable specifically because the evidence payload is new (VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md §1, §8 evidence visual exception).

visual_density.rationale: Axis, legend, and annotation chrome is functional rather than decorative, but must not accumulate ornamental detail beyond what the evidence requires (ARTICLE-ILLUSTRATION-ROUTING.md §2.1, §12 renderer integrity).

text_policy.complexity_ceiling: As many exact labels, axis values, or citations as the evidence dimensions require, but every one must be traceable to source data — never plausible-looking generated text (IMAGE-TEXT-RENDERING-PROFILES.md invariant 2). The whole artifact is deterministically authored rather than generative-raster-composited; hybrid_template is the nearest fit because structure and text are produced together, exactly.

composition.dominant_structure: A chart, table, timeline, or framework answering exactly one question (schemas/artifact-plan.schema.json spec.form, spec.question).
composition.chrome_level: as required by the evidence form; never padded for visual completeness

audience_adaptation.domain-expert: Legend optional; may show raw units, uncertainty bands, or unglossed methodology notes.
audience_adaptation.general-reader: Legend always shown and explained, not merely present (audience/general-reader.json-style default).
audience_adaptation.beginner-learner: Legend always shown and explained; expand every axis/unit term on first use.
audience_adaptation.child-upper-elementary: Usually skip; if used, the legend cannot be load-bearing and axis literacy must not be assumed (audience/child-upper-elementary.json modality_effects.visual).

renderer_preference.rule: A generated raster image must not impersonate computed evidence. Exact values, axes, dates, citations, rankings, or statistical comparisons must never ride on a generative model (IMAGE-GENERATION.md §1, §2; ARTICLE-ILLUSTRATION-ROUTING.md §2.1). Hybrid is tolerated only for a non-evidentiary illustrative frame placed around a deterministic evidence core; generative alone is never an acceptable route for this artifact.

readability_gate.rationale: Body-placed evidence visuals inherit the SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §5 mobile-gate principle, and the artifact-plan spec.feedback_point discipline requires the visual to remain inspectable, not merely present.

split_rule.rule: One question per visual — schemas/artifact-plan.schema.json spec.question is singular by construction. If a candidate evidence visual tries to answer two questions, split into two visuals rather than overlaying a second axis or series family (mirrors SUENGJ-ARTICLE-IMAGE-FAMILIES.md §6 one-plate-one-question).

acceptance: every value is traceable to verified claims or source data
passes the VISUAL-INFORMATION-GAIN.md §8 evidence exception test rather than merely restating the prose conclusion
the plan's feedback_point is stated: what it would mean if the visual does not show what was expected
reject: a generative-only route asked to carry exact values
more than one question answered on a single plate
